synopsis: PSNR measures image or field similarity using pixel-matched pairs; higher scores mean greater image fidelity, but these metrics assess appearance and structure rather than perception or decision-software behavior [f4802, f12930, f14791]. Viewpoint changes substantially reduce reported fidelity: XLD's synthetic CARLA benchmark drops from 30.87 dB at zero lateral shift to 19.17 dB at 4 m, while Para-Lane's real-data results fall from 22.99 dB in the recorded lane to 17.05 and 16.26 dB in adjacent lanes [f4001, f4003]. EUVS (2025) reports average PSNR reductions of 24.6% for translation, 25.6% for rotation and 30.6% for both; MV²'s August 2026 results show drone-trained scenes falling from 29.13 to 10.36 dB when viewed from a car [f4005, f4008]. Method and evaluation choices matter: EmerNeRF reaches 24.80 dB at XLD's 4 m shift, and MV²'s PVG car-to-scooter scores range from 14.72 dB without masks to 24.29 dB with ground-truth dynamic masks [f4002, f3890, f3891, f3892]. Diffusion repair improves Para-Lane two-lane results to 19.47 dB but still trails roughly 23 dB on the recorded path; generative novel-view methods report only 13.19–20.82 dB on Waymo in a 2026 preprint, which the corpus characterizes as low fidelity for safety testing and in tension with validation 'data machine' claims [f4013, f3821, f3822, f4330]. These benchmarks provide on-road or synthetic CARLA evidence, not a demonstrated heavy off-road validation result, and PSNR alone does not establish perception or decision-system validity [f4001, f4003, f4008, f3821, f14791].
